name: PassRole viability must keep CRITICAL for an {other}-shaped same-account role glob co-located with a concrete FOREIGN role (S2-passrole-allstmts iter-4, axis 1)
note: Fail-open of the SAME class as the statement-ORDER / ARN-spelling demotions, reached through an {other}-shaped PassRole target. ROLE_ARN_PARTS_RE only pins a concrete arn:...:role/<name>; a same-account token WITHOUT the literal ':role/' - arn:<subjectAcct>:role* / :r* / :role?* / :* / a leading-wildcard - parsed as {other}, and resourceReachesSubject returned a flat false for {other}. So a co-located CONCRETE foreign role (concreteSpecific.length>0) drove a confident critical->medium PASSROLE_CROSS_ACCOUNT_INCOMPATIBLE demotion and, because 'role*' also evades the WILDCARD-RESOURCE backstop (its head does not START with a wildcard), no high finding survived -> scan exit 0 CLEAN on a fully-viable, wildcard-scoped, same-account PassRole grant (threat-model T8). In AWS IAM 'arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role*' (and 'r*', 'role?*', ':*') glob-match every same-account role ARN. FIX: an {other} token now REACHES the subject when, read as an IAM wildcard glob, it COULD name a role ARN in the subject's own account+partition (a bounded, non-fixed-probe glob-produces-prefix decision) - so a viable same-account glob keeps the path CRITICAL and never lets a co-located foreign role demote it. Each `variant` is co-located IN THE SAME Pass statement with a concrete foreign role; analyze() must stay critical with NO confident demotion code and scan() must gate at exit 1 (never exit 0 CLEAN). `orderings` proves resource-order and statement-order independence; a canonical control confirms no over-correction.
